sentences.text:
The case of the claimants is briefly as follows:
a.
The claimants are the parents of Sri Bellamkonda Perumallaa Dasu (hereinafter referred to as 'the deceased').

On 14.05.2004, while the deceased was proceeding as a pillion rider on T.V.S. Victor motor cycle bearing No.AP 7 N7922 of the 1st respondent, he met with an accident due to the rash and negligent driving of the 1st respondent.
He died while undergoing treatment on 24.05.2004 as a result of the injuries suffered in the accident.
The deceased was aged about 19 years at the time of the accident.
He was earning Rs.3,000/- per month as a tailor and spending the same for the petitioners who were dependents on him.
The Tadepalligudem Town police station registered a case in Crime No.161 of 2004 under Section 338 I.P.C. and later it was altered to Section 304-A I.P.C.
The claimants sought compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- with interest at 12% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of realization and costs.
b. The 1st respondent remained ex parte.

c. The 2nd respondent / owner of the moped filed written statement denying the allegations and further stating that the vehicle was insured with the 3rd respondent and therefore, he is not personally liable to pay compensation.
BSB, J d.

The 3rd respondent filed written statement denying the allegations and also the liability and further stating that the claimants have to prove all the facts asserted by them and also that the 1st respondent had a valid driving licence as on the date of the accident.
It was further contended that the policy of insurance did not cover the risk of a pillion rider and therefore, it is not liable to pay any compensation.
4. In support of their claim, the claimants examined PWs 1 and 2 and exhibits A1 to A8 were marked.
PW1 is the first petitioner and PW2, Sri Reddy Yallarao, is an eyewitness to the accident.

Exhibit A1 is the attested copy of F.I.R. in Crime No.161 of 2004, exhibit A2 is the attested copy of altered F.I.R. in crime No.161 of 2004, exhibit A3 is the attested copy of charge sheet, exhibit A4 is the attested copy of P.M. report, exhibit A5 is the attested copy of M.V.I. report, exhibit A6 is the bunch of medical bills worth Rs.12,970/-, exhibit A7 is the discharge summary of D.Perumalla Das and exhibit A8 is the original C.T scan report.

On behalf of the respondents, RW1, Sri C.V.D.Prasad,
was examined and exhibit B1, copy of policy of Crime vehicle No.AP 07 N 7922 was marked.
5. After hearing both parties, the Tribunal found that the accident in question was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the 1st respondent.

The Tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs.1,91,700/- with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of realization and costs and directed the 1st and 2nd respondents to pay the same to the claimants.
The petition against the 3 rd respondent / insurance company was dismissed.

6. Aggrieved by the award and the decree, this appeal was filed by the claimants mainly contending that the insurance company shall be BSB, J made liable to pay the compensation as the seating capacity of the vehicle is two as per exhibit B1, insurance policy, which was categorically admitted by Bellamkonda Bhujanga Rao Anr vs Gatti Megharaju 2 Ors on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188246564/
2 RW1, the employee of the insurance company.

sentences.text: Insofar as the quantum of compensation is concerned, it was contended that the Tribunal erroneously assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.1,800/- instead of Rs.3,000/- per month and also that the Tribunal ought to have granted compensation of Rs.12,900/- under medical bills marked as exhibit A6 and that the multiplier adopted by the Tribunal is incorrect.
7. In spite of service of notice, the 1st respondent has not appeared before this Court.
Moreover, the 1st respondent remained ex parte before the Tribunal as well.
The appeal against the 2nd respondent was dismissed for default as per the order, dated 08.07.2016.
8. Heard learned counsel for the appellants and the learned counsel for the 3rd respondent.
9. The main grievance of the claimants is dismissal of the claim against the insurance company.
10. The learned counsel for the appellants contended that the insurance company is liable as the policy of insurance under exhibit B1 shows seating capacity of the vehicle as two.

11. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the respondent No.3 submitted that the insurance company is not liable to cover the risk unless separate premium is paid for a pillion rider, whereas,
in the present case, the premium paid is only for driver-cum-owner and that the Tribunal had rightly considered the contentions of both parties on this aspect and the appeal is liable to be dismissed.
BSB, J 12.
Merely because the seating capacity is two for the vehicle insured, it does not mean that the liability under the policy would cover two persons under the Act policy.
A separate premium is required to be paid for a pillion rider and in the absence of such premium, there is no liability to the insurance company.

It cannot be even treated as mere violation of term of policy so as to fasten liability on the insurance company to first pay and then recover the amount from the insured as was argued by the learned counsel for the appellants.
As such, this Court does not see any reason to interfere with the findings of the Tribunal regarding the liability of the 3 rd respondent.

13. Insofar as quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal ought to have applied the multiplier applicable to the deceased instead of the multiplier applicable to the age of the 2nd petitioner / mother.
As such, '18' is the relevant multiplier as per the decision of the Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors1.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After applying the multiplier '18', the annual contribution of the deceased to the claimants comes to Rs.14,400 X 18 = 2,59,200/-.

That apart, the amount of compensation granted @ Rs.2,500/- towards loss of estate is too low and as such, the compensation under this head is enhanced to Rs.15,000/- as the claim was assessed under Section 166 of the M.V. Act.
The amount of compensation of Rs.2,000/- awarded towards funeral expenses is too low and the same can be raised to Rs.10,000/-.

Since the claim made for medical expenditure under exhibit A6 for Rs.12,900/- is not on high side in view of the injuries suffered by the deceased, the Tribunal ought to have allowed the same AIR 2009 SC 3104 BSB, J Bellamkonda Bhujanga Rao Anr vs Gatti Megharaju 2 Ors on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188246564/
3 instead of dismissing it by too much rigid approach as the claim covered by the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation.

1 Loss of dependency 2,59,200=00  2 Loss of estate 15,000=00
3 Funeral expenses 10,000=00  4 Medical Bills 12,900=00

Total 2,97,100=00 Thus, the claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.2,97,100/-.
14.

Accordingly, the respondents 1 and 2 are directed to pay the enhanced compensation of Rs.1,05,400/- jointly and severally to the appellants / claimants with interest at the rate of 9% per annum on the enhanced amount of compensation from the date of filing of the appeal till the date of payment.
The enhanced compensation shall be paid within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
15. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part enhancing the amount of compensation while dismissing the appeal against the 3 rd respondent.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
